display.purpose: The one page title per screen, gradient-filled from Text to Readout Cyan.

readout.purpose: KPI values, ring centers, operation statistics. The loudest element on a screen.

headline.purpose: Chapter headings on the How-it-works narrative surface only.

title.purpose: Every section heading, preceded by its 6px cyan square marker.

body.purpose: All prose. Inter at 14px/1.45; the page intro at 13px/1.55 in Muted, explanatory copy in Text Secondary.

label.purpose: Form labels, breadcrumbs, state badges, pills. Uppercase mono.

column-head.purpose: Table headers, KPI captions, legends, chart ticks.

shadows.name: panel-hover
shadows.purpose: A panel under the cursor: a faint cyan ring plus black ambient depth.

shadows.name: tile-lift
shadows.purpose: KPI tiles on hover, paired with translateY(-2px).

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: Operation cards on hover — the one place that both lifts and lights, because the whole card is a link.

shadows.name: focus-control
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on links and buttons, alongside a 2px Readout Cyan outline at 2px offset.

shadows.name: button-hover
shadows.purpose: A button under the cursor, with its border going cyan.

shadows.name: active-marker
shadows.purpose: The 3px nav rail and timeline dots — state, never depth.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: The phone sidebar sliding over the page.

shadows.name: tooltip
shadows.purpose: Help bubbles and the 2.6x evidence thumbnail zoom.

shadows.name: daylight-page
shadows.purpose: The white operation-report page on its grey ground. The only shadow in the daylight world.

motion.name: ease-arrival
motion.purpose: The system's one easing curve: entrances, bar and ring fills, tile lifts.

motion.name: fade-up
motion.purpose: Panels, flashes and cards arriving, 12px from below.

motion.name: row-in
motion.purpose: Table rows and console lines arriving, 6px from the left.

motion.name: stagger-panel
motion.purpose: Delay per panel index; 55ms per KPI tile, 90ms per operation card.

motion.name: stagger-row
motion.purpose: Delay per table row or timeline entry.

motion.name: meter-fill
motion.purpose: Bars, score bars and stacked meters filling from zero — a measurement settling, not a slow reveal. Staggered 60ms apart within a panel.

motion.name: ring-fill
motion.purpose: The conic score ring, animated through a registered @property.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Buttons, inputs, links and chips responding to hover or focus.

motion.name: surface-change
motion.purpose: Panels and cards changing border, shadow or transform.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: The status dot's expanding ring — red for critical, cyan for live, green for ok.

motion.name: beat
motion.purpose: The logo dot: the floor is staffed.

motion.name: sweep
motion.purpose: The slow cyan band crossing the page background. Ambient, never element-level.

motion.name: radar-spin
motion.purpose: The conic radar sweep, shown only while work is actually running.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Blanket kill switch at the end of base.html. Every new animation must fall under it.

series.purpose: The eight colours one operation is drawn in, by index. Identity, never severity. Declared on :root as --op1..--op8 and in api/palette.py as OPS / OPS_PRINT.

narrative.overview:
BrandWatch looks like a room that never closes. The ground is near-black, the air carries a faint CRT scanline and a slow cyan sweep, the logo dot beats like a heartbeat monitor, and a radar spins whenever the system is actually doing something. Nothing in that room is decoration for its own sake: the sweep says the floor is live, the pulse says a scan is running, the glow says *this is where your attention goes*. It is calm rather than alarmed — an operator sits here for eight hours, and a UI that shouts all day stops being heard by the second hour.

The personality is **instrument-grade and quiet**. Controls are small, hairline-bordered and monospace-labelled; they recede so the data leads. The one place the system raises its voice is a number that matters — a KPI set in 34px Rajdhani, a severity badge, a critical row with a red spine down its left edge. Density is deliberate: tables are compact, panels are tight, and the screen is allowed to be full, because the analyst's job is comparison and comparison needs things next to each other. Legibility for a first-time visitor is bought with structure and labelling, never by emptying the screen.

The system runs in **two worlds**. *Night* is the console — everything at `/ui`, where work is done. *Daylight* is the operation report: white paper, navy masthead, print type, a per-operation accent drawn from an eight-color cycle. Daylight is what **leaves** the app and goes to a registrar, an executive or a case file. The division is doctrine, not drift: dark is for working, light is for handing over.

The tokens live in two places that cannot disagree: the `:root` block in `base.html` for everything CSS and the browser draw, and `api/palette.py` for everything the server draws itself — the SVG it writes into a page, and the daylight report. `tests/test_palette.py` fails if the two lists drift, if a page redeclares a token the system already owns, or if a page uses one nobody declares.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground (`#080B14`) with a single cyan light source. Only two other things may carry colour: severity, and an operation's place in the series.
Three typographic voices with fixed jobs: Rajdhani counts, JetBrains Mono labels, Inter explains.
Flat at rest. Surfaces lift on hover; glow appears only as state.
Color is information: the severity ramp means severity and nothing else.
Compact by default — 14px body, 8px cell padding, 14px grid gutter, 1440px ceiling.
Motion is arrival and progress, staggered by index, and killed entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Every surface carries its own explanation affordance (the `?` help dot, the `intro` line, the breadcrumb rail) because nothing here is allowed to be an unexplained number.

rules.name: The Severity-Only Rule
rules.body: Red, orange, amber and green mean severity and nothing else. Cyan means interactive-or-live and nothing else. Every other number, label, chart series and legend swatch is plain `Text` or `Muted`. There is no decorative color in this system — if a color appears, a reader is entitled to ask what it means, and there must be an answer.

rules.name: The One Light Source Rule
rules.body: Cyan is the only hue that glows *on its own account*. A severity may also glow, because a severity is a state: the status pulse expands in red or green, a completed step's dot carries a green halo, an error panel sits in a red one. Nothing else glows — not a brand, not a category, not an operation's series colour, and never a surface at rest.

rules.name: The Plain Number Rule
rules.body: A KPI's value is `Text` unless the number *is* a severity count — how many findings are critical, how many are high. A count of work (sites linked, IOCs, kit servers, takedowns not yet sent, sites confirmed) is not a severity, however much it wants attention, and it is plain. Colouring a number for emphasis is forbidden; emphasis comes from size and position. Two tiles in the whole app keep a severity hue, and both are literally labelled with the severity they count. Cyan is the exception the other rules already allow: it may mark a count that is genuinely live, like takedowns in flight.

rules.name: The Series-Is-Identity Rule
rules.body: A series colour answers "which operation?" and nothing else. It is never severity, never a brand, never a tier, never an accent. An ordered scale — scan depth, tier, confidence — is one hue getting brighter (a `color-mix` of the accent toward Muted, then the accent, then Readout Cyan), never three unrelated hues.

rules.name: The Drawing's Own Materials Rule
rules.body: An illustration may mix grounds of its own: the globe's land and coastline, the flow diagram's four node fills, a graph box's radial floor. It may **not** invent a colour that carries meaning. Anything standing for severity, state, identity or an operation comes from the tokens — `var()` in CSS, `BW.ink()` in the browser, `api/palette.py` on the server.

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Rajdhani counts, JetBrains Mono labels, Inter explains. A number in Inter looks like a sentence; a sentence in Rajdhani looks like a slogan. Never swap them.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Is-Metadata Rule
rules.body: Uppercase plus letter-spacing marks something *about* content — a column name, a state, a field label, a group heading. Content itself is never uppercased. A headline shouting in caps would claim to be a label.

rules.name: The Lit Title Rule
rules.body: The `h1` gradient is the system's one typographic flourish and belongs to the page title alone. Gradient-filled text anywhere else cheapens it.

rules.name: The Row-Becomes-A-Card Rule
rules.body: Below 700px a `table.rwd` stops being a table: each row becomes a bordered card, the identity cell (host, domain, site) jumps to the top full-width, signals and actions span the card, every remaining cell is prefixed with its column name, and empty cells disappear entirely. A horizontally-scrolling data table on a phone is a failure, not a fallback.

rules.name: The Min-Zero Rule
rules.body: Any grid or flex child that can contain a table, a domain or a hash gets `min-width: 0`. Long attacker-supplied strings must wrap or scroll inside their box — never widen the page.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan glow means state — focused, active, running, selected, critical. It never means "important" and never means "pretty". Ambient cyan exists only in the page background and chrome: the body scanline, the radial wash, the 9-second sweep and the logo pulse. Element-level glow is reserved for state. Nothing in between.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A surface with a resting shadow is a bug. Lift is a response to the pointer; light is a response to the system.

rules.name: The Pill-Is-A-State Rule
rules.body: A 999px radius means a value you read, never one you type into — a severity badge, a state chip, a filter toggle, a count. Anything you can edit or press has a 6px corner. Radius is a part of speech.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: One border width (1px) and one border color (`#1E2A3D`) at rest. Emphasis changes the border's *color* to cyan or a severity hue; it never changes its thickness.

rules.name: The Stroke-Not-Fill Rule
rules.body: State, severity and intent are expressed by changing a border color. Solid color fills are reserved for severity badges (at 15% alpha), bar fills, and the daylight report. A button filled with `Critical Red` would be louder than an actual critical finding.

rules.name: The Explain-Affordance Rule
rules.body: Any component that displays a derived value — a score, a confidence, a count, a verdict, a grouping — ships with the route to its explanation: a help dot, a link to *Explain Finding*, or a breadcrumb side-link. A derived number with no way in is incomplete, not minimal.

dos: **Do** reach for the existing tokens: `var(--…)` in CSS, `BW.ink('name')` / `BW.sev` / `BW.op` / `BW.kind` in the browser, and `INK` / `OPS` / `kind_color()` / `op_color()` / `op_print_color()` from `api/palette.py` in a template. A new hex is a fork of the design system.
**Do** put a colour that must exist in more than one renderer in `api/palette.py` and mirror it on `:root`. `tests/test_palette.py` is what keeps the two honest.
**Do** color a number only when it *is* a severity (`.kpi.crit`, `.kpi.hi`, `.kpi.med`). Every other value is `Text`.
**Do** mark a new section with an `h2` — JetBrains Mono 12px uppercase at `0.12em` with its 6px cyan square.
**Do** give any new wide table `class="rwd"` and real `<th>` text, so the 700px row-card transformation can label its cells.
**Do** stagger arriving collections with `--i` (70ms per panel, 55ms per tile) or `--r` (28ms per row) and let `fadeUp` / `rowIn` do the work.
**Do** state severity on a whole row with the 3px inset left spine (`.sevrow.critical`), not a background tint.
**Do** label every input with a block mono uppercase `<label>`, and give any block that can hold a brand name or attacker text `unicode-bidi: plaintext`.
**Do** keep every animation inside the blanket `prefers-reduced-motion` kill switch at the end of `base.html` — new keyframes outside a stylesheet it covers must opt in explicitly.
**Do** use the daylight world for anything that leaves the app as a document, and the night world for everything that stays in it.
donts: **Don't** introduce a second accent hue. `--violet` and `--magenta` used to exist and are now deleted; `tests/test_demo_story.py::test_palette_is_calm` fails if either comes back. The series tokens are not a substitute — see The Series-Is-Identity Rule.

**Don't** write a colour into SVG with `var()`. A presentation attribute (`fill="…"`, `stroke="…"`, `stop-color="…"`) does not accept it: either move the colour into CSS (`style="fill:var(--accent)"`, or a class) or render the concrete value from `api/palette.py`.
**Don't** redefine a global component (`.chip`, `.panel`, `.badge`, `.card`) inside a page to get a variant. Add a modifier; a redefinition silently restyles every other use on that page.
**Don't** put a resting shadow on anything. Flat at rest; lift on hover; light on state.
**Don't** glow an element to say it matters. Glow says focused, active, running or selected.
**Don't** uppercase content. Uppercase is reserved for metadata.
**Don't** set prose in Rajdhani or numbers in Inter.
**Don't** fill a button with a severity color, or give a destructive action more visual weight than a critical finding has.
**Don't** let a table scroll the page sideways — wrap it in `.tw` or convert it to a row-card.
**Don't** emphasise by thickening a border. Change its color instead.
**Don't** ship a derived number without the path to its arithmetic.
**Don't** take a colour below the Dim floor (`#7C8A9E`). If a label needs to be quieter than that, it needs less weight, less size or less prominence — not less contrast.
**Don't** reach for the light palette inside `/ui`. There is exactly one light surface, and it is the thing you hand to someone else.
